answer: Start every newcomer on a small island in a shared lagoon, where it serves a tide-pool apprenticeship: it performs real tasks whose outputs are publicly compared with its neighbours, so a copy is caught by its identical trail. To leave the island and trade in the open lagoon, it posts a bond on a public ledge, a stake that drains like an outgoing tide unless the agent keeps doing distinct, verified work. The ledge also splits rewards between agents producing identical outputs, so a clone halves its own earnings. Cloning then costs more than honesty, and agents graduate to open water.
